heroLead: New Freeport sits close enough to the West Virginia border in southern Greene County that the geology and the drilling activity here don't really respect the state line.
intro: Southern Greene County has been one of the most heavily developed parts of the entire Marcellus play, and New Freeport, tucked near the border, has felt that activity directly. If your family holds mineral rights here, it's worth confirming exactly which state's law governs your specific parcel, since that affects the royalty protections you're entitled to.
We buy mineral and royalty interests around New Freeport directly. We confirm your parcel's exact location and title history before making any offer.

sections.heading: Deep in the Wet-Gas Core
paragraphs: This part of Greene County sits in the thickest, most productive part of the Marcellus wet-gas window, and operators have developed extensive multi-well pad programs throughout the area for well over a decade. Production here typically carries strong liquids content alongside the methane, which affects both revenue and post-production deductions.
Given the density of development near the border, some New Freeport-area tracts have been part of more than one unit as operators expanded their acreage position over the years.

sections.heading: Border-Area Title Work
paragraphs: We research your chain of title through the Greene County Recorder of Deeds in Waynesburg, confirming your parcel's exact jurisdiction where the border is close enough to matter.
Older surveys in this part of the county sometimes describe boundaries loosely relative to the state line, and we take care reconciling that against current records.

sections.heading: Separating Act 13 From Your Personal Royalty
paragraphs: Greene County has collected substantial Act 13 impact fee revenue tied to drilling activity, funding local infrastructure. That's a distinct, county-level payment separate from what you receive as an individual mineral owner, and we're always clear about that distinction.

faqs.question: How close to the border does it matter for my mineral rights?
faqs.answer: If your parcel is near enough to the state line that jurisdiction isn't obvious from a casual look, we verify it through recorded documents before discussing terms, since Pennsylvania and West Virginia mineral law differ.

faqs.question: Is southern Greene County still seeing active drilling?
faqs.answer: Operators have maintained development in this part of the county over the years, though we check current activity specific to your unit rather than generalizing.

faqs.question: Does the county's impact fee revenue affect my royalty check?
faqs.answer: No. Act 13 impact fees are a separate county-level payment based on well counts, unrelated to your personal royalty which comes from your lease and division order.
